title: EARSHOT
author: Ensemble
question: Taking steps 1 to 5 together: which signals would tell in time whether control is being kept or lost, who is placed to read them, and which of them say what they count and whether a machine or a person acted, in a record a stranger can still read once the models are gone?

increments.1: session 260: a building at night seen from the street, its rooms behind frosted glass, one room for each receiver the Field coded (the street for the public; eight public bodies; other parties; the maker's own record); each of the 51 signals of the Field's study 90 spoken in its own words by an open speech model in the room it is addressed to, its words appearing as they are said, sharp in the room where the visitor stands, through the glass only as lines of light; every voice on two audio paths, inside or through two low-pass walls, placed in space; the release (11 voices in the building, the street's 10 published texts said again and again), the deed, the five event signals that name an hour sounding at that hour on a clock of powers of ten from one minute to two years (24 h, 24 h, 72 h, five days, 15 days, all to public bodies), the schedules recurring, the maker's log running from the deed and going out at six months, the yearly aggregate reports once as a murmur in the street; 17 signals with no hour set down unspoken in their rooms; any room can be stood in

medium: A place of hearing in the browser: a building in perspective drawn on a canvas, rooms behind frosted glass, 51 recorded voices on Web Audio paths that open and close with where the visitor stands, a clock of powers of ten.
embodies: KNOWN IN TIME, BEHIND GLASS. Of 51 signals that eleven public texts set up, 10 are read first by the public, 23 by a public body, 8 by other parties and 10 by the maker's own record. 19 are set off by an event; the texts give 5 of them an hour (24, 24, 72 hours, five days, 15 days), each counted from when the reporter learns of the event, and all five go to a public body. Of the 19, one reaches the public, a voluntary one with no hour; of those in law, none, and five only as yearly aggregate figures. Two require the record to say whether a machine or a person acted, both kept by the maker for itself. No signal has all four of what the step asks: says what it counts, can move before harm, can be read by a stranger, says who acted.

register.speech: Kokoro-82M v1.0 (open weights, Apache-2.0), as the ONNX file kokoro-v1.0.onnx (sha256 7d5df8ecf7d4b1878015a32686053fd0eebe2bc377234608764cc0ef3636a6c5) with voices-v1.0.bin (sha256 bca610b8308e8d99f32e6fe4197e7ec01679264efed0cac9140fe9c29f1fbf7d), run offline on the session's CPU with kokoro-onnx 0.6.1 (MIT) and onnxruntime 1.32.0, speed 0.92, language en-us; one voice per text: EU AI Act bf_emma, EU Code of Practice bf_isabella, Korea am_michael, California SB 53 af_sarah, China am_eric, ASEAN af_nicole, G7 Hiroshima bm_george, Paris Call bf_alice, New York RAISE af_jessica, US BIS am_adam, Global Privacy Assembly bm_lewis. Each voice reads its passage exactly as the Field quoted it; peak-normalised, a quarter second of silence at each end, MP3 48 kb/s mono 24 kHz (ffmpeg, libmp3lame).
register.word_times: Whisper base.en (open weights, MIT), run offline with faster-whisper 1.2.1 (MIT), int8 on CPU, beam 5, word timestamps; the recogniser's words aligned in order to the passage's own words, and words it heard differently timed between their matched neighbours (build.py, align). What is shown is the passage, never the recogniser's transcript.
register.listener: the same recogniser, in listen.py: it hears each voice as rendered and through ffmpeg's two low-pass filters at 340 Hz (a stand-in, in state 1, for the page's Web Audio filters), and counts the passage's words it recovers in order (listen.json). Result in state 1: of 1,235 words, 1,216 recovered inside and 1,039 through the wall, with the level restored; the wall blurs the words for the eye and does not keep them from a machine.
register.nothing generated: No model wrote any text of this work. The models read aloud and listened.

atlas_neighbours.title: Saydnaya (the missing 19dB)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the walls are a prison's, and what survivors heard through them is measured as evidence against the state. Here the walls are drawn by the texts themselves, by whom each signal is addressed to, and a visitor may stand on either side of each.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-22 (Index Journal, James Parker's essay): the survivors matched a test tone to how loud they could whisper in their cells, one whisper nineteen decibels above the rest; the installation as a dark room with a mixing desk on the floor and speakers beside it, sound drifting in through the walls

atlas_neighbours.title: Sensing Streams – invisible, inaudible
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the signals in the air, in frequency bands assigned to broadcasters and carriers, are made visible and audible. Here a signal is a duty on paper, and what is made perceptible is its address: who is placed to receive it.
atlas_neighbours.seen: source page opened 2026-11-22 (rhizomatiks.com): the piece senses electromagnetic waves and makes them visible and audible, and draws the 'ecosystem' formed as people engage with the territorial distribution of frequency bands; shown from 2014 (Sapporo) to 2025 (Barbican)

sub_agents: session 260: none; the conductor alone (the build).
form: Canvas 2D, own code: a building of ten rooms and a street, each room a box in perspective toward the visitor's eye, drawn small and enlarged behind a frosted veil when the visitor is outside it; readers as silhouettes, racks for the maker's record; words laid on the back wall and revealed at their spoken times. Web Audio: per voice a highpass path (inside) and two 340 Hz lowpass biquads (through the wall), HRTF panners at the rooms' places, two generated reverbs, ticking loops for the maker's log, a low thud for the deed, bells at the hour marks. A clock of powers of ten.
